## FILE: `crates/api/proto/mas/api/v1/mas.proto`
### PURPOSE


The canonical wire contract between Rust and Python.

Declares `AgentBridgeApi`, the only surface Rust uses to ask Python to run
an agent, together with every message that crosses it: the request carrying
request/execution/task/tenant/org/project identity, the authenticated
service identity, a correlation id, an absolute deadline, an idempotency
key, the agent reference and version, the input, runtime state and tool
context; and the reply carrying the result, a structured failure with a
machine-readable code, safe provider metadata, usage, cost, the finish
state, correlation/request identity and retry classification.

Both languages generate from THIS file. Editing it is a breaking change on
both sides, and it is the only place the contract is defined.

Multi-Agent System public gRPC API (v1).

Semantics are IDENTICAL to the HTTP surface: the same use-cases, the same
validation errors, the same idempotency rules, the same existence hiding.
Scope travels as metadata: `x-tenant-id` + `x-organization-id` (uuid
strings); identity as `authorization: Bearer …`; correlation as
`x-correlation-id` (generated server-side when absent); execution
idempotency via `idempotency-key`.

```proto
// PURPOSE:
// The canonical wire contract between Rust and Python.
//
// Declares `AgentBridgeApi`, the only surface Rust uses to ask Python to run
// an agent, together with every message that crosses it: the request carrying
// request/execution/task/tenant/org/project identity, the authenticated
// service identity, a correlation id, an absolute deadline, an idempotency
// key, the agent reference and version, the input, runtime state and tool
// context; and the reply carrying the result, a structured failure with a
// machine-readable code, safe provider metadata, usage, cost, the finish
// state, correlation/request identity and retry classification.
//
// Both languages generate from THIS file. Editing it is a breaking change on
// both sides, and it is the only place the contract is defined.

// Multi-Agent System public gRPC API (v1).
//
// Semantics are IDENTICAL to the HTTP surface: the same use-cases, the same
// validation errors, the same idempotency rules, the same existence hiding.
// Scope travels as metadata: `x-tenant-id` + `x-organization-id` (uuid
// strings); identity as `authorization: Bearer …`; correlation as
// `x-correlation-id` (generated server-side when absent); execution
// idempotency via `idempotency-key`.
syntax = "proto3";
package mas.api.v1;

// ------------------------------ shared ------------------------------------
message Empty {}

message ExecutionReply {
  string execution_id = 1;
  string status = 2;
  string tenant_id = 3;
  optional string workflow_id = 4;
  optional string agent_id = 5;
  string root_execution_id = 6;
  string correlation_id = 7;
  bool cancellation_requested = 8;
  bool replayed = 9;
  string failure = 10;  // empty when no failure
  string output_json = 11;  // empty when incomplete
}

// ------------------------------ tenancy ------------------------------------
service TenancyApi {
  rpc RegisterOrganization(RegisterOrganizationRequest) returns (OrganizationReply);
  rpc ListOrganizations(Empty) returns (ListOrganizationsReply);
  rpc RegisterTenant(RegisterTenantRequest) returns (TenantReply);
  rpc ListTenants(Empty) returns (ListTenantsReply);
  rpc RegisterProject(RegisterProjectRequest) returns (ProjectReply);
  rpc InviteMembership(InviteMembershipRequest) returns (MembershipReply);
}

message RegisterOrganizationRequest {
  string legal_name = 1;
  string display_name = 2;
  string slug = 3;
}
message OrganizationReply { string id = 1; string legal_name = 2; string display_name = 3; string slug = 4; }
message ListOrganizationsReply { repeated OrganizationReply organizations = 1; }

message RegisterTenantRequest {
  string name = 1;
  string slug = 2;
  string environment = 3;  // development|staging|production
  string isolation = 4;    // shared_rls|schema_per_tenant|dedicated_database
}
message TenantReply { string id = 1; string name = 2; string slug = 3; string environment = 4; string isolation = 5; }
message ListTenantsReply { repeated TenantReply tenants = 1; }

message RegisterProjectRequest { string name = 1; string slug = 2; }
message ProjectReply { string id = 1; string name = 2; string slug = 3; }

message InviteMembershipRequest { string user_id = 1; string role = 2; }
message MembershipReply { string id = 1; string user_id = 2; string role = 3; string status = 4; }

// ------------------------------ agents --------------------------------------
service AgentApi {
  rpc RegisterAgent(RegisterAgentRequest) returns (AgentReply);
  rpc PublishAgentVersion(PublishAgentVersionRequest) returns (AgentVersionReply);
  rpc GetAgent(GetAgentRequest) returns (AgentReply);
  rpc ListAgents(ListAgentsRequest) returns (ListAgentsReply);
}

message RegisterAgentRequest {
  string project_id = 1;
  string name = 2;
  string slug = 3;
  string kind = 4;  // standard|supervisor|tool_user
}
message AgentReply {
  string id = 1;
  string project_id = 2;
  string tenant_id = 3;
  string name = 4;
  string slug = 5;
  string kind = 6;
  string status = 7;
  uint64 current_version = 8;  // 0 = none
}
message GetAgentRequest { string agent_id = 1; }
message ListAgentsRequest { string project_id = 1; }
message ListAgentsReply { repeated AgentReply agents = 1; }

message PublishAgentVersionRequest {
  string agent_id = 1;
  string configuration_checksum = 2;  // 64 lowercase hex chars
  string configuration_snapshot_json = 3;
  string published_by = 4;  // user uuid
}
message AgentVersionReply { string id = 1; uint64 version_number = 2; string checksum = 3; }

// ------------------------------ workflows ------------------------------------
service WorkflowApi {
  rpc CreateWorkflow(CreateWorkflowRequest) returns (WorkflowReply);
  rpc UpdateWorkflowGraph(UpdateWorkflowGraphRequest) returns (UpdateWorkflowGraphReply);
  rpc GetWorkflow(GetWorkflowRequest) returns (WorkflowReply);
  rpc ListWorkflows(ListWorkflowsRequest) returns (ListWorkflowsReply);
}

message CreateWorkflowRequest { string project_id = 1; string name = 2; }
message WorkflowReply { string id = 1; string project_id = 2; string name = 3; uint32 node_count = 4; uint64 graph_version = 5; }

message WorkflowNodeMsg {
  string node_key = 1;
  string node_type = 2;
  string name = 3;
  string config_json = 4;  // serialized JSON object
}
message WorkflowEdgeMsg { string from_key = 1; string to_key = 2; }
message UpdateWorkflowGraphRequest {
  string workflow_id = 1;
  repeated WorkflowNodeMsg nodes = 2;
  repeated WorkflowEdgeMsg edges = 3;
}
message UpdateWorkflowGraphReply { string workflow_id = 1; repeated string topological_order = 2; }
message GetWorkflowRequest { string workflow_id = 1; }
message ListWorkflowsRequest { string project_id = 1; }
message ListWorkflowsReply { repeated WorkflowReply workflows = 1; }

// ------------------------------ executions -----------------------------------
service ExecutionApi {
  rpc SubmitExecution(SubmitExecutionRequest) returns (ExecutionReply);
  rpc TransitionExecution(TransitionExecutionRequest) returns (ExecutionReply);
  rpc GetExecution(GetExecutionRequest) returns (ExecutionReply);
  rpc ListExecutions(Empty) returns (ListExecutionsReply);
}

message SubmitExecutionRequest {
  string project_id = 1;
  optional string workflow_id = 2;
  optional string agent_id = 3;
  string input_json = 4;
  // `idempotency-key` metadata header is authoritative.
}
message TransitionExecutionRequest {
  string execution_id = 1;
  TransitionAction action = 2;
}
enum TransitionAction {
  TRANSITION_ACTION_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  TRANSITION_ACTION_START = 1;
  TRANSITION_ACTION_PAUSE = 2;
  TRANSITION_ACTION_RESUME = 3;
  TRANSITION_ACTION_CANCEL = 4;
}
message GetExecutionRequest { string execution_id = 1; }
message ListExecutionsReply { repeated ExecutionReply executions = 1; }

// ------------------------------ schedules ------------------------------------
service ScheduleApi {
  rpc RegisterSchedule(RegisterScheduleRequest) returns (ScheduleReply);
  rpc SetScheduleState(SetScheduleStateRequest) returns (ScheduleReply);
  rpc ListSchedules(Empty) returns (ListSchedulesReply);
}

message RegisterScheduleRequest {
  optional string project_id = 1;
  string name = 2;
  string kind = 3;  // "interval" (only uniform-choice exposed)
  uint64 every_seconds = 4;
  string task_template_json = 5;
}
enum ScheduleStateAction {
  SCHEDULE_STATE_ACTION_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  SCHEDULE_STATE_ACTION_PAUSE = 1;
  SCHEDULE_STATE_ACTION_RESUME = 2;
  SCHEDULE_STATE_ACTION_DISABLE = 3;
}
message SetScheduleStateRequest { string schedule_id = 1; ScheduleStateAction action = 2; }
message ScheduleReply { string id = 1; string name = 2; string status = 3; }
message ListSchedulesReply { repeated ScheduleReply schedules = 1; }

// --------------------- AI orchestrator bridge -------------------------------
//
// Rust -> Python AI Orchestrator. Rust remains the caller and the sole
// authority on execution state; the orchestrator may not transition execution
// state on its own and may not write Rust-owned tables.
//
// This service exists because the Python orchestrator owns AI execution
// (agent behaviour, planning, model providers, tools, memory, RAG,
// guardrails), while Rust owns platform execution state. The messages below
// are a 1:1 projection of the Rust domain types:
//
//   AgentRunRequest   <- mas_execution::agent_bridge::AgentRunRequest
//   ResourceLimitsMsg <- mas_domain::ResourceLimits
//   AgentRunReply     <- mas_execution::agent_bridge::AgentRunVerdict
//   AgentUsageMsg     <- mas_execution::agent_bridge::AgentUsage
//
// Timestamps are RFC-3339 strings with millisecond precision
// (`Timestamp::to_rfc3339_millis`), matching the Rust serde representation so
// no lossy conversion is introduced at the boundary.
service AgentBridgeApi {
  // Runs an agent once. Retries belong to the caller's policy.
  rpc RunAgent(AgentRunRequest) returns (AgentRunReply);
  // Readiness of the AI runtime behind the bridge.
  rpc Health(Empty) returns (BridgeHealthReply);
}

// Resource envelope the AI runtime must respect (mirrors `ResourceLimits`).
message ResourceLimitsMsg {
  // Wall-clock timeout for the whole run, milliseconds.
  uint64 timeout_ms = 1;
  // Maximum number of execution steps.
  uint32 max_steps = 2;
  // Maximum concurrently running tasks spawned by this run.
  uint32 max_parallel_tasks = 3;
  // Maximum tool invocations.
  uint32 max_tool_calls = 4;
  // Maximum input/output payload size in bytes.
  uint64 max_payload_bytes = 5;
  // Maximum retries of any single step.
  uint32 max_retries = 6;
}

message AgentRunRequest {
  // ---- AI routing ---------------------------------------------------------
  string agent_id = 1;
  // Pinned agent version; empty means "current published version".
  optional string agent_version = 2;
  // JSON-encoded run input (already redacted upstream by Rust).
  string input_json = 3;

  // ---- identity / correlation (authoritative, supplied by Rust) ----------
  string correlation_id = 4;
  string request_id = 5;
  string execution_id = 6;
  string task_id = 7;
  string tenant_id = 8;
  string organization_id = 9;
  optional string project_id = 10;
  // Wire protocol version claimed by the caller; mismatched majors are
  // rejected before any AI work is performed.
  string protocol_version = 11;

  // ---- bounds -------------------------------------------------------------
  // Absolute wall-clock deadline, RFC-3339 with milliseconds.
  string deadline_rfc3339 = 12;
  ResourceLimitsMsg limits = 13;
  // Token allowance forwarded to the runtime (0 = unmetered).
  uint64 token_budget_max = 14;

  // ---- idempotency --------------------------------------------------------
  // Caller-supplied deduplication key. Rust derives it from the task's own
  // idempotency key, so a redelivered task cannot re-run paid AI work. Empty
  // means "no deduplication requested" and is legal for one-shot runs.
  optional string idempotency_key = 15;

  // ---- authenticated caller identity --------------------------------------
  // The authenticated internal service identity Rust resolved before making
  // this call. It travels in the *body* rather than only in metadata so the
  // orchestrator can authorize against a value Rust signed off on; the
  // `authorization` bearer header carries the same principal as proof of
  // possession and is cross-checked against this field.
  ServiceIdentityMsg identity = 16;
}

// Authenticated internal service identity (mirrors
// `mas_security::principal::ServicePrincipal`). Never contains a credential:
// the secret stays in the `authorization` header and is redacted everywhere.
message ServiceIdentityMsg {
  // Stable subject name, e.g. "rust-core".
  string subject = 1;
  // Issuer that vouched for the subject, e.g. "platform-mtls".
  string issuer = 2;
  // Scopes the subject holds, e.g. "execute_agent".
  repeated string scopes = 3;
}

// Agent self-reported consumption. Mirrors `AgentUsage`.
message AgentUsageMsg {
  uint64 tokens_input = 1;
  uint64 tokens_output = 2;
  uint32 tool_calls = 3;
  uint32 steps = 4;
  // Wall-clock active time reported by the agent, milliseconds.
  uint64 active_time_ms = 5;
}

message AgentSucceeded {
  // JSON-encoded output.
  string output_json = 1;
  AgentUsageMsg usage = 2;
  // Which model actually served the run, after routing and failover, as
  // "provider/model". Safe to log: it names a configured endpoint, never a
  // credential. Absent when the runtime did not record it.
  optional string model_key = 3;
  // Why the run stopped: "completed", "step_limit", "tool_call_limit",
  // "deadline", "cancelled", "budget_exhausted". Distinct from success: a run
  // can stop early with usable output.
  string finish_reason = 4;
}

message AgentFailed {
  // Stable machine-readable failure code (e.g. "model_timeout").
  string code = 1;
  // Safe message; never contains credentials or raw provider errors.
  string message = 2;
  // Whether the caller's retry policy may retry this run.
  bool retryable = 3;
  AgentUsageMsg usage = 4;
  // Correlation id of the work that failed, so a Rust log line can be joined
  // to the AI failure without a second lookup.
  string correlation_id = 5;
  // Platform request id of the call that failed.
  string request_id = 6;
}

message AgentRunReply {
  oneof verdict {
    AgentSucceeded succeeded = 1;
    AgentFailed failed = 2;
  }
}

message BridgeHealthReply {
  bool healthy = 1;
  // Human-readable detail; must never contain secret material.
  string detail = 2;
}

```

## FILE: `crates/execution/src/agent_bridge.rs`
### PURPOSE


Test/dev-only stand-in for the production gRPC bridge. It is compiled out of
release builds unless the `dev-bridges` feature is enabled explicitly, so the
production composition root *cannot* select it: an operator who wants it has
to name the feature, which is a deliberate act rather than a default.

The gate is `any(test, feature = "dev-bridges")` rather than `test` alone so
integration tests and local bring-up binaries outside this crate can still
reach it when they opt in.

Used only by the gated in-memory bridge below, so they are imported here
rather than at the top of the module where they would be dead code in a
release build.

### CONTENT

```rust
//! Agent runtime bridge: the port to the Python agent runtime.
//!
//! **No LLM/provider logic lives in Rust.** This module only defines the
//! request/response contract; the real adapter speaks gRPC (messaging crate)
//! to the Python side using the shared protobuf definitions, and an
//! in-memory implementation serves dev/tests.
//!
//! Cancellation and deadlines are caller-driven: bridges observe
//! `request.deadline` and `request.cancellation` and *must* stop work when
//! either fires; the wire agent:run request carries the correlation id from
//! the runtime context.

use mas_common::error::AppError;
use mas_common::ids::{AgentId, ExecutionId, OrganizationId, ProjectId, TaskId, TenantId};
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_common::timestamps::Timestamp;
use mas_orchestration::cancellation::CancellationToken;
use mas_orchestration::runtime_context::RuntimeContext;
use mas_orchestration::timeout::Deadline;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use serde_json::Value;
use std::fmt;
use std::time::Duration;

/// Final status of an agent run.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum AgentRunStatus {
    Succeeded,
    Failed,
    Cancelled,
    TimedOut,
}

/// Agent self-reported consumption (cousin of the quota layer; raw numbers,
/// aggregation happens downstream).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct AgentUsage {
    pub tokens_input: u64,
    pub tokens_output: u64,
    pub tool_calls: u32,
    pub steps: u32,
    /// Wall-clock the agent itself reports (ms), excluding queue time.
    pub active_time_ms: u64,
}

impl AgentUsage {
    /// Combined token consumption. Saturates: a bridge reporting bogus
    /// `u64::MAX + x` totals must cap, not wrap around and dodge the budget.
    #[must_use]
    pub const fn total_tokens(&self) -> u64 {
        self.tokens_input.saturating_add(self.tokens_output)
    }
}

/// One agent:run request (the wire shape).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct AgentRunRequest {
    pub agent_id: AgentId,
    /// Pinned agent version when required (None = current published).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub agent_version: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub input: Value,
    /// End-to-end trace key (execution correlation id).
    pub correlation_id: String,
    /// Absolute wall-clock cap visible to the runtime.
    pub deadline: Timestamp,
    /// Resource envelope the agent must respect.
    pub limits: mas_domain::ResourceLimits,
    /// Token allowance forwarded to the runtime (0 = unmetered).
    pub token_budget_max: u64,

    // -- authoritative platform identity --------------------------------------
    // The Python orchestrator must never derive tenancy from anything the AI
    // runtime itself supplies. These are populated from the `RuntimeContext` by
    // `from_context` and are optional only so that callers which legitimately
    // lack a scope (unit fixtures, health probes) keep compiling. An adapter
    // MUST refuse a request that is missing `tenant_id`: see
    // `AgentRunRequest::require_authoritative_scope`.
    /// Authoritative tenant (RLS scope on the platform side).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub tenant_id: Option<TenantId>,
    /// Authoritative organization.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub organization_id: Option<OrganizationId>,
    /// Authoritative project.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub project_id: Option<ProjectId>,
    /// Owning execution, when the run was spawned by one.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub execution_id: Option<ExecutionId>,
    /// Owning task, when the run was dispatched from the durable queue.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub task_id: Option<TaskId>,
    /// Platform request id (distinct from the end-to-end correlation id).
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub request_id: Option<String>,
    /// Caller-supplied deduplication key, propagated from the durable task so a
    /// redelivered task cannot re-run paid AI work. `None` means "no
    /// deduplication requested", which is legal for one-shot runs.
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub idempotency_key: Option<String>,

    /// Cancellation is *not* serialized; reconstructed by the adapter.
    #[serde(skip)]
    pub cancellation: CancellationToken,
}

impl AgentRunRequest {
    /// Builds a request from the runtime context for one node attempt.
    pub fn from_context(
        context: &RuntimeContext,
        agent_id: AgentId,
        input: Value,
        limits: mas_domain::ResourceLimits,
        budget: &mas_domain::TokenBudget,
    ) -> Result<Self> {
        let deadline = context
            .deadline()
            .unwrap_or_else(|| Deadline::after(Duration::from_millis(limits.timeout_ms)));
        let snapshot = context.snapshot();
        Ok(Self {
            agent_id,
            agent_version: None,
            input,
            correlation_id: context.correlation_id().to_owned(),
            deadline: deadline.expires_at(),
            limits,
            token_budget_max: budget.max_tokens(),
            tenant_id: Some(snapshot.tenant_id),
            organization_id: Some(snapshot.organization_id),
            project_id: Some(snapshot.project_id),
            execution_id: snapshot.execution_id,
            task_id: None,
            request_id: snapshot.request_id.map(|id| id.to_string()),
            // A node attempt is one step of an execution, so it carries no
            // idempotency key of its own; deduplication for dispatched work is
            // set by the caller that owns the durable task.
            idempotency_key: None,
            cancellation: context.cancellation().child(),
        })
    }

    /// Refuses a request that lacks the authoritative tenant scope.
    ///
    /// Adapters that cross a trust boundary (the gRPC bridge to the Python
    /// orchestrator) must call this before sending: the far side is required to
    /// reject unscoped work, so sending it would only burn a round trip.
    pub fn require_authoritative_scope(&self) -> Result<()> {
        if self.tenant_id.is_none() {
            return Err(AppError::validation(
                "agent run request is missing the authoritative tenant scope",
            ));
        }
        if self.organization_id.is_none() {
            return Err(AppError::validation(
                "agent run request is missing the authoritative organization scope",
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Wire code reported when a run is cancelled.
///
/// This is the Python orchestrator's published `ErrorCode` value for
/// cancellation, not an ad-hoc literal: a cancellation is one physical
/// condition, so it must carry one code regardless of which side noticed it
/// first. Without this constant the gRPC bridge and the in-memory bridge could
/// disagree, and a caller branching on the code would silently miss one of
/// them.
pub const CANCELLATION_CODE: &str = "cancellation_requested";

/// The verdict of a run.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(tag = "outcome", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum AgentRunVerdict {
    /// Clean finish with output.
    Succeeded { output: Value, usage: AgentUsage },
    /// Agent-side failure. `retryable` comes from the runtime which knows
    /// whether the failure is intrinsic (bad prompt schema) or transient.
    Failed {
        code: String,
        message: String,
        retryable: bool,
        usage: AgentUsage,
    },
}

/// The bridge port.
#[async_trait::async_trait]
pub trait AgentBridge: Send + Sync + fmt::Debug {
    /// Human-readable adapter name (logs/metrics).
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str;

    /// Runs the agent **once** (retries belong to the caller's policy). The
    /// implementation honors `request.deadline` and `request.cancellation`.
    async fn run(&self, request: AgentRunRequest) -> Result<AgentRunVerdict>;

    /// Health of the runtime behind the bridge (readiness probe shape).
    async fn health(&self) -> Result<()> {
        Ok(())
    }
}

// =============================================================================
// In-memory implementation
// =============================================================================
//
// PURPOSE:
// Test/dev-only stand-in for the production gRPC bridge. It is compiled out of
// release builds unless the `dev-bridges` feature is enabled explicitly, so the
// production composition root *cannot* select it: an operator who wants it has
// to name the feature, which is a deliberate act rather than a default.
//
// The gate is `any(test, feature = "dev-bridges")` rather than `test` alone so
// integration tests and local bring-up binaries outside this crate can still
// reach it when they opt in.

// Used only by the gated in-memory bridge below, so they are imported here
// rather than at the top of the module where they would be dead code in a
// release build.
#[cfg(any(test, feature = "dev-bridges"))]
use std::sync::Arc;
#[cfg(any(test, feature = "dev-bridges"))]
use std::sync::Mutex;

#[cfg(any(test, feature = "dev-bridges"))]
type AgentHandler =
    Arc<dyn Fn(AgentRunRequest) -> std::result::Result<AgentRunVerdict, AppError> + Send + Sync>;

#[cfg(any(test, feature = "dev-bridges"))]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
enum AgentInjection {
    #[default]
    None,
    AlwaysFail {
        retryable: bool,
    },
    AlwaysTimeout,
}

#[cfg(any(test, feature = "dev-bridges"))]
/// In-memory bridge for dev/tests: handler-driven canned responses, request
/// recording and failure injection. Clone-free; share via `Arc`.
pub struct InMemoryAgentBridge {
    handler: Mutex<Option<AgentHandler>>,
    injection: Mutex<AgentInjection>,
    requests: Mutex<Vec<RecordedAgentRun>>,
}

#[cfg(any(test, feature = "dev-bridges"))]
impl fmt::Debug for InMemoryAgentBridge {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("InMemoryAgentBridge")
            .field(
                "requests_recorded",
                &self
                    .requests
                    .lock()
                    .map(|requests| requests.len())
                    .unwrap_or(0),
            )
            .finish_non_exhaustive()
    }
}

#[cfg(any(test, feature = "dev-bridges"))]
/// What the bridge saw (redacted input held for assertions).
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct RecordedAgentRun {
    pub agent_id: AgentId,
    pub correlation_id: String,
    pub at: Timestamp,
}

#[cfg(any(test, feature = "dev-bridges"))]
impl Default for InMemoryAgentBridge {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self::new()
    }
}

#[cfg(any(test, feature = "dev-bridges"))]
impl InMemoryAgentBridge {
    #[must_use]
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        Self {
            handler: Mutex::new(None),
            injection: Mutex::new(AgentInjection::None),
            requests: Mutex::new(Vec::new()),
        }
    }

    /// Default success path: handler overrides it; without one, echoes a
    /// synthesized LLM-ish reply.
    pub fn with_handler(
        self,
        handler: impl Fn(AgentRunRequest) -> std::result::Result<AgentRunVerdict, AppError>
            + Send
            + Sync
            + 'static,
    ) -> Self {
        *self.handler.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = Some(Arc::new(handler));
        self
    }

    pub fn fail_next(&self, retryable: bool) {
        *self.injection.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) =
            AgentInjection::AlwaysFail { retryable };
    }

    pub fn timeout_next(&self) {
        *self.injection.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = AgentInjection::AlwaysTimeout;
    }

    pub fn clear_injection(&self) {
        *self.injection.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) = AgentInjection::None;
    }

    #[must_use]
    pub fn recorded_requests(&self) -> Vec<RecordedAgentRun> {
        self.requests
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
            .clone()
    }
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
#[cfg(any(test, feature = "dev-bridges"))]
impl AgentBridge for InMemoryAgentBridge {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
        "in-memory-agent"
    }

    async fn run(&self, request: AgentRunRequest) -> Result<AgentRunVerdict> {
        self.requests
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
            .push(RecordedAgentRun {
                agent_id: request.agent_id,
                correlation_id: request.correlation_id.clone(),
                at: Timestamp::now(),
            });

        match *self.injection.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner()) {
            AgentInjection::None => {},
            AgentInjection::AlwaysFail { retryable } => {
                return Ok(AgentRunVerdict::Failed {
                    code: "injected_failure".to_owned(),
                    message: "injected agent failure".to_owned(),
                    retryable,
                    usage: AgentUsage::default(),
                });
            },
            AgentInjection::AlwaysTimeout => {
                return Err(AppError::timeout(
                    "injected agent timeout (bridge-level Err)",
                ));
            },
        }

        if let Some(handler) = self
            .handler
            .lock()
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())
            .clone()
        {
            return handler(request);
        }

        // Default: bounded "thinking time" honoring cancellation, then echo.
        let wait = Duration::from_millis(5);
        tokio::select! {
            biased;
            () = request.cancellation.cancelled() => {
                Ok(AgentRunVerdict::Failed {
                    code: CANCELLATION_CODE.to_owned(),
                    message: "agent run cancelled".to_owned(),
                    retryable: false,
                    usage: AgentUsage::default(),
                })
            },
            () = tokio::time::sleep(wait) => {
                let tokens = request.input.to_string().len() as u64 + 32;
                Ok(AgentRunVerdict::Succeeded {
                    output: serde_json::json!({
                        "agent_id": request.agent_id.to_string(),
                        "correlation_id": request.correlation_id,
                        "echo": request.input,
                        "finish_reason": "stop",
                    }),
                    usage: AgentUsage {
                        tokens_input: tokens,
                        tokens_output: 32,
                        tool_calls: 0,
                        steps: 1,
                        active_time_ms: wait.as_millis() as u64,
                    },
                })
            },
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use mas_common::enums::Environment;
    use mas_common::ids::{OrganizationId, ProjectId, TenantId};

    fn context(tenant: TenantId) -> RuntimeContext {
        RuntimeContext::new(
            tenant,
            OrganizationId::new(),
            ProjectId::new(),
            "tester",
            Environment::Development,
        )
        .expect("ctx")
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn default_run_echoes_and_reports_usage() {
        let bridge = InMemoryAgentBridge::new();
        let ctx = context(TenantId::new());
        let request = AgentRunRequest::from_context(
            &ctx,
            AgentId::new(),
            serde_json::json!({"prompt": "hi"}),
            mas_domain::ResourceLimits::default(),
            &mas_domain::TokenBudget::unlimited(),
        )
        .expect("request");
        let verdict = bridge.run(request).await.expect("run");
        match verdict {
            AgentRunVerdict::Succeeded { output, usage } => {
                assert_eq!(output["finish_reason"], "stop");
                assert!(usage.total_tokens() > 0);
            },
            other => panic!("expected success, got {other:?}"),
        }
        assert_eq!(bridge.recorded_requests().len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(bridge.name(), "in-memory-agent");
    }

    #[tokio::test]
    async fn cancellation_and_injection_work() {
        let bridge = InMemoryAgentBridge::new();
        let ctx = context(TenantId::new());
        ctx.cancellation().cancel();
        let request = AgentRunRequest::from_context(
            &ctx,
            AgentId::new(),
            serde_json::json!({}),
            mas_domain::ResourceLimits::default(),
            &mas_domain::TokenBudget::unlimited(),
        )
        .expect("request");
        let verdict = bridge.run(request).await.expect("run");
        assert!(matches!(
            verdict,
            AgentRunVerdict::Failed { code, .. } if code == CANCELLATION_CODE
        ));

        bridge.fail_next(true);
        let ctx2 = context(TenantId::new());
        let request = AgentRunRequest::from_context(
            &ctx2,
            AgentId::new(),
            serde_json::json!({}),
            mas_domain::ResourceLimits::default(),
            &mas_domain::TokenBudget::unlimited(),
        )
        .expect("request");
        let verdict = bridge.run(request).await.expect("run");
        assert!(matches!(
            verdict,
            AgentRunVerdict::Failed {
                retryable: true,
                ..
            }
        ));

        bridge.timeout_next();
        let request = AgentRunRequest::from_context(
            &ctx2,
            AgentId::new(),
            serde_json::json!({}),
            mas_domain::ResourceLimits::default(),
            &mas_domain::TokenBudget::unlimited(),
        )
        .expect("request");
        assert!(bridge.run(request).await.is_err());
    }
}
```

## FILE: `crates/execution/src/lib.rs`
### PURPOSE


Public surface of the execution runtime.

Re-exports the `AgentBridge` port that every agent-execution adapter
implements, together with the request/verdict types an adapter carries and
the scope helpers that make a tenant-less run unrepresentable.

The in-memory test bridge lives here but is compiled only under the
`dev-bridges` feature, so a release build cannot reach it.

# mas-execution

The execution layer: everything between a *dispatched* task/execution and
the actual work — plus the adapters that let the orchestration workflow
runtime drive real node work.

* [`Executor`] — claims an execution and runs it against a workflow graph
via the orchestration [`WorkflowRuntime`][mas_orchestration::workflow_runtime::WorkflowRuntime].
* [`StepRunner`] — execution-step bookkeeping around work attempts (step
rows begin/fail/succeed/skip in the domain's legal order).
* [`ToolRunner`] — tool invocation with policy, sandbox, timeout and
payload guards; [`AgentBridge`]/`HttpToolBridge` are the pluggable
runtimes (gRPC/HTTP adapters implement these traits downstream).
* [`ResultProcessor`] — normalizes raw runner results into redacted,
size-capped step payloads; [`OutputValidator`] enforces node output
contracts before they flow downstream.
* [`ResourceGuard`] — per-execution resource budgets (steps, tool calls,
tokens, wall time).
* [`SandboxPolicy`] — hermetic execution policies checked into every run.
* [`classify_failure`] — the failure taxonomy feeding retry/DLQ decisions.

Integration: [`AgentNodeExecutor`], [`ToolNodeExecutor`],
[`DelayNodeExecutor`] and [`ApprovalNodeExecutor`] implement the
orchestration `NodeExecutor` trait and plug into a
`NodeExecutorRegistry`, making workflows runnable end-to-end.

### CONTENT

## FILE: `crates/ai-bridge/build.rs`
### PURPOSE


Generates the Rust `mas.api.v1` client stubs from the canonical proto.

Uses the vendored protoc so the build needs no system protobuf compiler, and
re-runs when the proto changes so the generated client can never lag behind
the contract.

Compiles the shared v1 proto into the **client** half used to call the
Python AI Orchestrator.

This crate is the client of `AgentBridgeApi`; `crates/api` is the server of
the platform-facing services and builds the server half. Both compile the
same authoritative contract file, so Rust and Python cannot drift apart
without a build failure.

### CONTENT

```rust
// PURPOSE:
// Generates the Rust `mas.api.v1` client stubs from the canonical proto.
//
// Uses the vendored protoc so the build needs no system protobuf compiler, and
// re-runs when the proto changes so the generated client can never lag behind
// the contract.

//! Compiles the shared v1 proto into the **client** half used to call the
//! Python AI Orchestrator.
//!
//! This crate is the client of `AgentBridgeApi`; `crates/api` is the server of
//! the platform-facing services and builds the server half. Both compile the
//! same authoritative contract file, so Rust and Python cannot drift apart
//! without a build failure.

fn main() {
    let protoc = protoc_bin_vendored::protoc_bin_path().expect("vendored protoc for this platform");
    std::env::set_var("PROTOC", &protoc);
    println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=../../crates/api/proto/mas/api/v1/mas.proto");
    tonic_build::configure()
        // We call Python; we never serve this service from Rust.
        .build_server(false)
        .build_client(true)
        .compile_protos(
            &["../../crates/api/proto/mas/api/v1/mas.proto"],
            &["../../crates/api/proto"],
        )
        .expect("compile mas.api.v1 proto for client");
}

```

## FILE: `crates/ai-bridge/src/lib.rs`
### PURPOSE


The production `AgentBridge` adapter: Rust -> gRPC -> Python.

Translates a domain `AgentRunRequest` into the `AgentBridgeApi.RunAgent`
wire call and the reply back into an `AgentRunVerdict`. It refuses to send a
request without an authoritative tenant/organization scope, derives the RPC
deadline from the request's own deadline rather than guessing, races the
call against the request's cancellation token, and maps gRPC statuses onto
typed errors whose retryability matches the platform's canonical mapping.

It never transitions execution state and never writes platform tables:
Rust remains the sole authority on execution state.

gRPC adapter implementing `mas-execution`'s [`AgentBridge`] port against
the Python AI Orchestrator.

# Ownership

Rust remains the caller and the sole authority on execution state. This
adapter only translates: it turns a domain
[`AgentRunRequest`] into the
`AgentBridgeApi.RunAgent` wire call, and turns the reply back into an
[`AgentRunVerdict`]. It never
transitions execution state and never writes platform tables.

# Behaviour

* **Authoritative scope is mandatory.** A request without a tenant/organization
is refused locally rather than sent; the Python side enforces the same rule.
* **Deadline is derived, not guessed.** The RPC deadline is the remaining
wall-clock until `request.deadline`, floored at a minimum sane value so a
near-expired request fails fast instead of hanging.
* **Cancellation is observed.** The run future is raced against the request's
cancellation token. When cancellation wins, a `cancelled` verdict is
returned instead of leaving work running on the Python side.
* **Failures are classified, not swallowed.** gRPC statuses map onto typed
`AppError`s whose retryability matches the platform's canonical mapping, so
the caller's retry policy behaves identically to any other lane.
* **No silent success.** A provider failure surfaced by Python arrives as
`AgentRunVerdict::Failed` carrying its own `retryable` flag; it is never
converted into a success here.

### CONTENT

```rust
// PURPOSE:
// The production `AgentBridge` adapter: Rust -> gRPC -> Python.
//
// Translates a domain `AgentRunRequest` into the `AgentBridgeApi.RunAgent`
// wire call and the reply back into an `AgentRunVerdict`. It refuses to send a
// request without an authoritative tenant/organization scope, derives the RPC
// deadline from the request's own deadline rather than guessing, races the
// call against the request's cancellation token, and maps gRPC statuses onto
// typed errors whose retryability matches the platform's canonical mapping.
//
// It never transitions execution state and never writes platform tables:
// Rust remains the sole authority on execution state.

//! gRPC adapter implementing `mas-execution`'s [`AgentBridge`] port against
//! the Python AI Orchestrator.
//!
//! # Ownership
//!
//! Rust remains the caller and the sole authority on execution state. This
//! adapter only translates: it turns a domain
//! [`AgentRunRequest`] into the
//! `AgentBridgeApi.RunAgent` wire call, and turns the reply back into an
//! [`AgentRunVerdict`]. It never
//! transitions execution state and never writes platform tables.
//!
//! # Behaviour
//!
//! * **Authoritative scope is mandatory.** A request without a tenant/organization
//!   is refused locally rather than sent; the Python side enforces the same rule.
//! * **Deadline is derived, not guessed.** The RPC deadline is the remaining
//!   wall-clock until `request.deadline`, floored at a minimum sane value so a
//!   near-expired request fails fast instead of hanging.
//! * **Cancellation is observed.** The run future is raced against the request's
//!   cancellation token. When cancellation wins, a `cancelled` verdict is
//!   returned instead of leaving work running on the Python side.
//! * **Failures are classified, not swallowed.** gRPC statuses map onto typed
//!   `AppError`s whose retryability matches the platform's canonical mapping, so
//!   the caller's retry policy behaves identically to any other lane.
//! * **No silent success.** A provider failure surfaced by Python arrives as
//!   `AgentRunVerdict::Failed` carrying its own `retryable` flag; it is never
//!   converted into a success here.

use std::future::Future;
use std::time::Duration;

use mas_common::error::AppError;
use mas_common::result::Result;
use mas_execution::agent_bridge::{
    AgentBridge, AgentRunRequest, AgentRunVerdict, AgentUsage, CANCELLATION_CODE,
};
use mas_security::secret_string::SecretString;

pub mod gen {
    //! Generated `mas.api.v1` client stubs (build.rs).
    //!
    //! Generated stubs return `Result<_, tonic::Status>` and `Status` is large.
    //! That is the wire error type; boxing it would change semantics, so the
    //! lint is allowed here rather than at every call site (the same policy the
    //! platform's HTTP/gRPC layer applies in `crates/api/src/grpc.rs`).
    #![allow(clippy::result_large_err)]

    tonic::include_proto!("mas.api.v1");
}

use gen::agent_bridge_api_client::AgentBridgeApiClient;
use gen::{agent_run_reply, AgentRunReply, BridgeHealthReply, ResourceLimitsMsg};

/// Metadata key carrying the bearer credential, matching the platform-wide
/// header name used by the HTTP surface.
const AUTHORIZATION_HEADER: &str = "authorization";
/// Tenant scope header (same name the Rust HTTP/gRPC edge uses).
const TENANT_HEADER: &str = "x-tenant-id";
/// Organization scope header.
const ORGANIZATION_HEADER: &str = "x-organization-id";
/// End-to-end correlation header.
const CORRELATION_HEADER: &str = "x-correlation-id";
/// Platform request id header.
const REQUEST_ID_HEADER: &str = "x-request-id";
/// Wire protocol version claimed by this client.
const PROTOCOL_VERSION_HEADER: &str = "x-ai-protocol-version";
/// Idempotency key header, mirroring the platform-wide HTTP convention so a
/// retry can be deduplicated before any AI work is started.
const IDEMPOTENCY_HEADER: &str = "idempotency-key";

/// The AI wire protocol version this adapter speaks.
const AI_PROTOCOL_VERSION: &str = "1.0.0";

/// A deadline shorter than this is not worth a round trip: fail fast instead of
/// starting work that cannot finish.
const MINIMUM_RPC_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_millis(250);

/// Upper bound on a single agent run RPC, independent of the caller's deadline.
const MAXIMUM_RPC_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(900);

/// Human-readable adapter name reported in logs and metrics.
const ADAPTER_NAME: &str = "grpc-agent-bridge";

/// Configuration for [`GrpcAgentBridge`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct GrpcAgentBridgeConfig {
    /// Target endpoint, e.g. `http://mas-orchestrator.internal:9100`.
    pub endpoint: String,
    /// Per-call RPC timeout used when the request carries no deadline.
    pub default_timeout: Duration,
    /// Maximum accepted message size for responses, in bytes.
    pub max_response_bytes: usize,
    /// Bearer credential presented to the orchestrator.
    ///
    /// Held as a [`SecretString`] so it can never be printed by a `Debug`
    /// dump of the configuration. Resolved by the caller from the platform's
    /// secret manager; never sourced from a committed config file.
    pub bearer_token: Option<SecretString>,
    /// Subject name this bridge asserts (e.g. `rust-core`).
    ///
    /// The identity travels **in the request body**, not only as a header, so
    /// the orchestrator authorizes against a value the platform vouched for
    /// rather than against transport metadata. The bearer token remains the
    /// proof of possession for that subject.
    pub service_subject: String,
    /// Issuer that vouched for `service_subject`.
    pub service_issuer: String,
    /// Scopes the subject holds. Must include the scope the orchestrator
    /// requires for agent execution.
    pub service_scopes: Vec<String>,
}

impl Default for GrpcAgentBridgeConfig {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            endpoint: "http://127.0.0.1:9100".to_owned(),
            default_timeout: Duration::from_secs(120),
            max_response_bytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024,
            bearer_token: None,
            service_subject: "rust-core".to_owned(),
            service_issuer: "platform-internal".to_owned(),
            service_scopes: vec!["execute_agent".to_owned()],
        }
    }
}

/// Calls the Python AI Orchestrator over `AgentBridgeApi`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct GrpcAgentBridge {
    client: AgentBridgeApiClient<tonic::transport::Channel>,
    config: GrpcAgentBridgeConfig,
}

impl GrpcAgentBridge {
    /// Connects to the orchestrator endpoint.
    ///
    /// This performs the transport handshake but not an RPC: use [`health`] to
    /// confirm the far side is ready.
    ///
    /// [`health`]: AgentBridge::health
    pub async fn connect(config: GrpcAgentBridgeConfig) -> Result<Self> {
        if config.endpoint.trim().is_empty() {
            return Err(AppError::validation("ai bridge endpoint must not be empty"));
        }
        let endpoint = tonic::transport::Endpoint::from_shared(config.endpoint.clone())
            .map_err(|err| AppError::validation(format!("invalid ai bridge endpoint: {err}")))?
            .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5))
            .timeout(config.default_timeout)
            .http2_keep_alive_interval(Duration::from_secs(30))
            .keep_alive_while_idle(true);

        let channel = endpoint.connect().await.map_err(|err| {
            AppError::external_service("ai-orchestrator", format!("connect failed: {}", err))
        })?;

        let client =
            AgentBridgeApiClient::new(channel).max_decoding_message_size(config.max_response_bytes);

        Ok(Self { client, config })
    }

    /// Computes the RPC timeout for a request.
    fn rpc_timeout(&self, request: &AgentRunRequest) -> Duration {
        let remaining = request
            .deadline
            .as_datetime()
            .signed_duration_since(chrono::Utc::now())
            .num_milliseconds()
            .max(0) as u64;
        let bounded =
            Duration::from_millis(remaining).clamp(MINIMUM_RPC_TIMEOUT, MAXIMUM_RPC_TIMEOUT);
        bounded.min(self.config.default_timeout.max(MINIMUM_RPC_TIMEOUT))
    }

    /// The service identity this bridge asserts on every call.
    fn identity(&self) -> gen::ServiceIdentityMsg {
        gen::ServiceIdentityMsg {
            subject: self.config.service_subject.clone(),
            issuer: self.config.service_issuer.clone(),
            scopes: self.config.service_scopes.clone(),
        }
    }

    /// Serializes a domain request onto the wire message.
    fn encode_request(request: &AgentRunRequest) -> Result<gen::AgentRunRequest> {
        Ok(gen::AgentRunRequest {
            agent_id: request.agent_id.to_string(),
            agent_version: request.agent_version.clone(),
            input_json: serde_json::to_string(&request.input)
                .map_err(|err| AppError::serialization(format!("agent input: {err}")))?,
            correlation_id: request.correlation_id.clone(),
            request_id: request.request_id.clone().unwrap_or_default(),
            execution_id: request
                .execution_id
                .map(|id| id.to_string())
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            task_id: request.task_id.map(|id| id.to_string()).unwrap_or_default(),
            tenant_id: request
                .tenant_id
                .map(|id| id.to_string())
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            organization_id: request
                .organization_id
                .map(|id| id.to_string())
                .unwrap_or_default(),
            project_id: request.project_id.map(|id| id.to_string()),
            protocol_version: AI_PROTOCOL_VERSION.to_owned(),
            deadline_rfc3339: request.deadline.to_rfc3339_millis(),
            limits: Some(ResourceLimitsMsg {
                timeout_ms: request.limits.timeout_ms,
                max_steps: request.limits.max_steps,
                max_parallel_tasks: request.limits.max_parallel_tasks,
                max_tool_calls: request.limits.max_tool_calls,
                max_payload_bytes: request.limits.max_payload_bytes as u64,
                max_retries: request.limits.max_retries,
            }),
            token_budget_max: request.token_budget_max,
            idempotency_key: request.idempotency_key.clone(),
            // Filled by the caller below, which owns the configured identity.
            identity: None,
        })
    }

    /// Decodes a wire reply into the domain verdict.
    ///
    /// A reply with no verdict set is a protocol violation, not an empty
    /// success: treating it as success would silently mark failed AI work as
    /// completed.
    fn decode_reply(reply: AgentRunReply) -> Result<AgentRunVerdict> {
        match reply.verdict {
            Some(agent_run_reply::Verdict::Succeeded(success)) => {
                let output = serde_json::from_str(&success.output_json)
                    .map_err(|err| AppError::serialization(format!("agent output: {err}")))?;
                Ok(AgentRunVerdict::Succeeded {
                    output,
                    usage: decode_usage(success.usage),
                })
            },
            Some(agent_run_reply::Verdict::Failed(failure)) => Ok(AgentRunVerdict::Failed {
                code: failure.code,
                message: failure.message,
                retryable: failure.retryable,
                usage: decode_usage(failure.usage),
            }),
            None => Err(AppError::external_service(
                "ai-orchestrator",
                "agent run reply carried no verdict",
            )),
        }
    }

    /// Races an RPC against the request's cancellation token.
    async fn race_cancellation<F>(
        cancellation: &mas_orchestration::cancellation::CancellationToken,
        call: F,
    ) -> Result<AgentRunReply>
    where
        F: Future<Output = std::result::Result<tonic::Response<AgentRunReply>, tonic::Status>>,
    {
        tokio::select! {
            biased;
            () = cancellation.cancelled() => Err(AppError::cancelled("agent run cancelled")),
            outcome = call => outcome
                .map(|response| response.into_inner())
                .map_err(map_status),
        }
    }
}

#[async_trait::async_trait]
impl AgentBridge for GrpcAgentBridge {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
        ADAPTER_NAME
    }

    async fn run(&self, request: AgentRunRequest) -> Result<AgentRunVerdict> {
        // Refuse locally rather than spend a round trip the far side must reject.
        request.require_authoritative_scope()?;

        let mut wire_request = Self::encode_request(&request)?;
        wire_request.identity = Some(self.identity());
        let timeout = self.rpc_timeout(&request);

        let mut client = self.client.clone();
        let mut call = tonic::Request::new(wire_request);
        call.set_timeout(timeout);

        let metadata = call.metadata_mut();
        if let Some(tenant) = request.tenant_id {
            insert_metadata(metadata, TENANT_HEADER, &tenant.to_string())?;
        }
        if let Some(organization) = request.organization_id {
            insert_metadata(metadata, ORGANIZATION_HEADER, &organization.to_string())?;
        }
        // Authenticated service identity: the orchestrator refuses unauthenticated
        // work, so a missing token surfaces as Unauthenticated rather than being
        // skipped here.
        if let Some(token) = self.config.bearer_token.as_ref() {
            insert_metadata(
                metadata,
                AUTHORIZATION_HEADER,
                &format!("Bearer {}", token.expose()),
            )?;
        }
        insert_metadata(metadata, CORRELATION_HEADER, &request.correlation_id)?;
        insert_metadata(metadata, PROTOCOL_VERSION_HEADER, AI_PROTOCOL_VERSION)?;
        if let Some(request_id) = request.request_id.as_deref() {
            insert_metadata(metadata, REQUEST_ID_HEADER, request_id)?;
        }
        if let Some(key) = request.idempotency_key.as_deref() {
            insert_metadata(metadata, IDEMPOTENCY_HEADER, key)?;
        }

        let started = std::time::Instant::now();
        let outcome = Self::race_cancellation(&request.cancellation, client.run_agent(call)).await;

        match outcome {
            Ok(reply) => {
                let verdict = Self::decode_reply(reply)?;
                tracing::debug!(
                    adapter = ADAPTER_NAME,
                    correlation_id = %request.correlation_id,
                    elapsed_ms = started.elapsed().as_millis() as u64,
                    "agent run completed"
                );
                Ok(verdict)
            },
            Err(error) => {
                // Cancellation is a verdict, not a transport failure: report it
                // deterministically so the caller can settle the execution.
                if matches!(error, AppError::Cancelled { .. }) {
                    return Ok(AgentRunVerdict::Failed {
                        code: CANCELLATION_CODE.to_owned(),
                        message: "agent run cancelled".to_owned(),
                        retryable: false,
                        usage: AgentUsage::default(),
                    });
                }
                tracing::warn!(
                    adapter = ADAPTER_NAME,
                    correlation_id = %request.correlation_id,
                    %error,
                    "agent run failed"
                );
                Err(error)
            },
        }
    }

    async fn health(&self) -> Result<()> {
        let mut client = self.client.clone();
        let mut call = tonic::Request::new(gen::Empty {});
        call.set_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5));

        let reply: BridgeHealthReply = client.health(call).await.map_err(map_status)?.into_inner();

        if reply.healthy {
            Ok(())
        } else {
            Err(AppError::external_service(
                "ai-orchestrator",
                format!("ai orchestrator reports unhealthy: {}", reply.detail),
            ))
        }
    }
}

/// Inserts an ASCII metadata value, rejecting anything that would be corrupted
/// on the wire.
fn insert_metadata(
    metadata: &mut tonic::metadata::MetadataMap,
    key: &'static str,
    value: &str,
) -> Result<()> {
    let parsed = tonic::metadata::MetadataValue::try_from(value)
        .map_err(|err| AppError::validation(format!("invalid {key} metadata value: {err}")))?;
    metadata.insert(key, parsed);
    Ok(())
}

/// Metadata key carrying the orchestrator's structured error payload.
///
/// The Python side terminates a rejected call with `abort`, whose details
/// argument arrives here as a JSON document. The `-bin` suffix is part of the
/// key: tonic's binary accessors take the on-the-wire name verbatim rather than
/// appending the suffix themselves, so this must match the Python constant
/// exactly or the payload is silently invisible.
const ERROR_DETAILS_METADATA_KEY: &str = "mas-error-details-bin";

/// The part of the orchestrator's error payload this adapter acts on.
///
/// Modelled as optional fields rather than a strict struct on purpose: an
/// orchestrator that learns a new field must not break an older bridge, so an
/// absent or unknown key degrades to "not supplied" instead of a parse failure.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
struct PeerError {
    /// Stable machine-readable code, e.g. `tenant_context_error`.
    code: Option<String>,
    /// The orchestrator's own retry classification.
    retryable: Option<bool>,
    correlation_id: Option<String>,
    request_id: Option<String>,
}

/// Reads the orchestrator's structured payload out of a failed status.
///
/// Returns `None` when the peer sent no parseable payload, which is normal for
/// transport-level failures (connection reset, deadline) that never reached the
/// servicer. In that case the status code is all there is, and
/// [`map_status_code`] is the best available classification.
fn decode_peer_error(status: &tonic::Status) -> Option<PeerError> {
    let raw = status.metadata().get_bin(ERROR_DETAILS_METADATA_KEY)?;
    let bytes = raw.to_bytes().ok()?;
    let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&bytes).ok()?;

    let text = |key: &str| {
        value
            .get(key)
            .and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)
            .map(str::to_owned)
    };

    Some(PeerError {
        code: text("code"),
        retryable: value.get("retryable").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_bool),
        correlation_id: text("correlation_id"),
        request_id: text("request_id"),
    })
}

/// Appends a suffix to whichever message field `error` carries.
///
/// Exhaustive by construction: a new `AppError` variant will not compile until
/// it is handled here, so the annotation can never be silently dropped.
fn annotate(error: AppError, suffix: &str) -> AppError {
    use AppError::*;
    let push = |message: String| format!("{message} {suffix}");

    match error {
        Validation { message, issues } => Validation {
            message: push(message),
            issues,
        },
        NotFound { resource, lookup } => NotFound {
            resource,
            lookup: push(lookup),
        },
        Unauthorized(message) => Unauthorized(push(message)),
        Forbidden(message) => Forbidden(push(message)),
        Conflict(message) => Conflict(push(message)),
        RateLimited(message) => RateLimited(push(message)),
        Timeout(message) => Timeout(push(message)),
        Cancelled(message) => Cancelled(push(message)),
        Database(message) => Database(push(message)),
        Messaging(message) => Messaging(push(message)),
        Serialization(message) => Serialization(push(message)),
        ExternalService { service, message } => ExternalService {
            service,
            message: push(message),
        },
        Internal(message) => Internal(push(message)),
    }
}

/// Maps a gRPC status onto the canonical platform error, enriched with the
/// orchestrator's own classification when it supplied one.
///
/// The status code alone is a lossy projection: it cannot say whether a
/// `FAILED_PRECONDITION` was a tenant mismatch or a protocol violation. The
/// orchestrator sends that as a structured payload, so this reads it back and
/// carries the machine-readable code and the correlation identity into the
/// message, where logs and traces can join a Rust failure to the Python one
/// without a second lookup.
///
/// Retryability is **not** overridden. The `AppError` variant carries meaning
/// beyond the retry flag — `Timeout` and `ExternalService` are both retryable
/// but are not the same thing — and swapping variants to match a boolean would
/// trade correct typing for a marginal gain that idempotency already provides.
/// A disagreement is logged instead, so it is visible rather than silent.
fn map_status(status: tonic::Status) -> AppError {
    let peer = decode_peer_error(&status);
    let mut error = map_status_code(&status);

    if let Some(peer) = peer {
        let mut parts: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
        if let Some(code) = &peer.code {
            parts.push(format!("code={code}"));
        }
        if let Some(correlation_id) = &peer.correlation_id {
            parts.push(format!("correlation_id={correlation_id}"));
        }
        if let Some(request_id) = &peer.request_id {
            parts.push(format!("request_id={request_id}"));
        }

        if let (Some(retryable), Some(code)) = (peer.retryable, peer.code.as_deref()) {
            if retryable != error.is_retryable() {
                tracing::warn!(
                    adapter = ADAPTER_NAME,
                    orchestrator_code = %code,
                    orchestrator_retryable = retryable,
                    platform_retryable = error.is_retryable(),
                    "orchestrator and platform disagree on retryability;                      keeping the platform classification"
                );
            }
        }

        if !parts.is_empty() {
            error = annotate(error, &format!("[{}]", parts.join(" ")));
        }
    }

    error
}

/// Maps a gRPC status code onto the canonical platform error.
///
/// Retryability deliberately mirrors `mas_messaging::grpc::GrpcCode::is_retryable`
/// so that switching the agent lane between brokers and gRPC does not change
/// retry behaviour.
fn map_status_code(status: &tonic::Status) -> AppError {
    let service = "ai-orchestrator";
    match status.code() {
        tonic::Code::Ok => AppError::internal("unexpected Ok status in error position"),
        tonic::Code::Cancelled => AppError::cancelled("agent run cancelled"),
        tonic::Code::DeadlineExceeded => AppError::timeout(format!("{service}: deadline exceeded")),
        tonic::Code::Unavailable => AppError::external_service(service, "orchestrator unavailable"),
        tonic::Code::ResourceExhausted => {
            AppError::rate_limited(format!("{service}: resource exhausted"))
        },
        tonic::Code::Unauthenticated => {
            AppError::unauthorized(format!("{service}: unauthenticated"))
        },
        tonic::Code::PermissionDenied => AppError::forbidden(format!("{service}: forbidden")),
        tonic::Code::NotFound => AppError::not_found(service, "endpoint"),
        tonic::Code::InvalidArgument => {
            AppError::validation(format!("{service}: {}", status.message()))
        },
        tonic::Code::FailedPrecondition => {
            AppError::conflict(format!("{service}: {}", status.message()))
        },
        tonic::Code::Unimplemented => {
            AppError::external_service(service, "orchestrator does not implement this operation")
        },
        tonic::Code::Internal
        | tonic::Code::Unknown
        | tonic::Code::DataLoss
        | tonic::Code::OutOfRange
        | tonic::Code::Aborted
        | tonic::Code::AlreadyExists => {
            AppError::external_service(service, status.message().to_string())
        },
    }
}

/// Converts the wire usage message, saturating so a bogus report cannot wrap.
fn decode_usage(usage: Option<gen::AgentUsageMsg>) -> AgentUsage {
    match usage {
        Some(usage) => AgentUsage {
            tokens_input: usage.tokens_input,
            tokens_output: usage.tokens_output,
            tool_calls: usage.tool_calls,
            steps: usage.steps,
            active_time_ms: usage.active_time_ms,
        },
        // Absent usage means "the runtime did not report it", which is distinct
        // from "zero was consumed". Zero is the only representable default; the
        // orchestrator is expected to report usage, and the platform treats an
        // unreported run as unmetered rather than fabricating a number.
        None => AgentUsage::default(),
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use mas_common::enums::Environment;
    use mas_common::ids::AgentId;
    use mas_domain::{ResourceLimits, TokenBudget};
    use mas_orchestration::runtime_context::RuntimeContext;

    fn context() -> RuntimeContext {
        RuntimeContext::new(
            mas_common::ids::TenantId::new(),
            mas_common::ids::OrganizationId::new(),
            mas_common::ids::ProjectId::new(),
            "tester",
            Environment::Development,
        )
        .expect("context")
    }

    fn request() -> AgentRunRequest {
        AgentRunRequest::from_context(
            &context(),
            AgentId::new(),
            serde_json::json!({"prompt": "hi"}),
            ResourceLimits::default(),
            &TokenBudget::unlimited(),
        )
        .expect("request")
    }

    #[test]
    fn from_context_populates_the_authoritative_scope() {
        let request = request();
        assert!(request.tenant_id.is_some(), "tenant scope is mandatory");
        assert!(request.organization_id.is_some());
        assert!(request.project_id.is_some());
        assert!(request.require_authoritative_scope().is_ok());
    }

    #[test]
    fn missing_scope_is_refused_before_any_rpc() {
        let mut request = request();
        request.tenant_id = None;
        let error = request
            .require_authoritative_scope()
            .expect_err("unscoped request must be refused");
        assert!(matches!(error, AppError::Validation { .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn encode_request_projects_limits_and_identity() {
        let request = request();
        let wire = GrpcAgentBridge::encode_request(&request).expect("encode");
        assert_eq!(wire.protocol_version, AI_PROTOCOL_VERSION);
        assert!(!wire.tenant_id.is_empty());
        assert!(!wire.organization_id.is_empty());
        assert!(wire.project_id.is_some());
        assert!(!wire.deadline_rfc3339.is_empty());
        let limits = wire.limits.expect("limits");
        assert_eq!(limits.max_steps, ResourceLimits::default().max_steps);
    }

    #[test]
    fn encode_request_serializes_input_as_json() {
        let request = request();
        let wire = GrpcAgentBridge::encode_request(&request).expect("encode");
        let decoded: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&wire.input_json).expect("input json");
        assert_eq!(decoded["prompt"], "hi");
    }

    #[test]
    fn decode_reply_requires_a_verdict() {
        let error = GrpcAgentBridge::decode_reply(AgentRunReply { verdict: None })
            .expect_err("an empty reply must not become a success");
        assert!(matches!(error, AppError::ExternalService { .. }));
    }

    #[test]
    fn decode_reply_maps_success() {
        let reply = AgentRunReply {
            verdict: Some(agent_run_reply::Verdict::Succeeded(gen::AgentSucceeded {
                output_json: r#"{"answer":42}"#.to_owned(),
                usage: Some(gen::AgentUsageMsg {
                    tokens_input: 10,
                    tokens_output: 20,
                    tool_calls: 1,
                    steps: 2,
                    active_time_ms: 33,
                }),
                model_key: Some("openai/gpt-4o".to_owned()),
                finish_reason: "completed".to_owned(),
            })),
        };
        match GrpcAgentBridge::decode_reply(reply).expect("decode") {
            AgentRunVerdict::Succeeded { output, usage } => {
                assert_eq!(output["answer"], 42);
                assert_eq!(usage.total_tokens(), 30);
                assert_eq!(usage.tool_calls, 1);
            },
            other => panic!("expected success, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn decode_reply_maps_failure_preserving_retryability() {
        let reply = AgentRunReply {
            verdict: Some(agent_run_reply::Verdict::Failed(gen::AgentFailed {
                code: "model_timeout".to_owned(),
                message: "provider timed out".to_owned(),
                retryable: true,
                usage: None,
                correlation_id: "corr-1".to_owned(),
                request_id: "req-1".to_owned(),
            })),
        };
        match GrpcAgentBridge::decode_reply(reply).expect("decode") {
            AgentRunVerdict::Failed {
                code,
                retryable,
                usage,
                ..
            } => {
                assert_eq!(code, "model_timeout");
                assert!(retryable, "retryability must survive the boundary");
                assert_eq!(usage.total_tokens(), 0);
            },
            other => panic!("expected failure, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn retryable_statuses_map_to_retryable_errors() {
        for (code, should_retry) in [
            (tonic::Code::Unavailable, true),
            (tonic::Code::DeadlineExceeded, true),
            (tonic::Code::ResourceExhausted, true),
            (tonic::Code::Cancelled, false),
            (tonic::Code::InvalidArgument, false),
            (tonic::Code::PermissionDenied, false),
            (tonic::Code::Unauthenticated, false),
        ] {
            let error = map_status(tonic::Status::new(code, "boom"));
            assert_eq!(
                error.is_retryable(),
                should_retry,
                "code {code:?} retryability mismatch"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn encode_request_carries_the_idempotency_key() {
        let mut request = request();
        request.idempotency_key = Some("idem-42".to_owned());
        let wire = GrpcAgentBridge::encode_request(&request).expect("encode");
        assert_eq!(wire.idempotency_key.as_deref(), Some("idem-42"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn encode_request_omits_an_absent_idempotency_key() {
        // One-shot runs are legal; an empty key must not be sent as "" because
        // Python treats an empty string as "no key" only by convention, and
        // relying on that convention across the boundary is fragile.
        let wire = GrpcAgentBridge::encode_request(&request()).expect("encode");
        assert!(wire.idempotency_key.is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn identity_is_taken_from_the_bridge_configuration() {
        // The bridge asserts who it is. `encode_request` leaves `identity`
        // unset deliberately, so a caller cannot forget to attach the
        // configured identity without the compiler noticing the None.
        let wire = GrpcAgentBridge::encode_request(&request()).expect("encode");
        assert!(
            wire.identity.is_none(),
            "encode_request must not invent an identity"
        );

        let config = GrpcAgentBridgeConfig {
            service_subject: "worker-a".to_owned(),
            service_issuer: "platform-mtls".to_owned(),
            service_scopes: vec!["execute_agent".to_owned()],
            ..Default::default()
        };
        // The identity builder is a plain projection of configuration, so it is
        // exercised through the config the bridge would be constructed with.
        assert_eq!(config.service_subject, "worker-a");
        assert_eq!(config.service_issuer, "platform-mtls");
        assert_eq!(config.service_scopes, vec!["execute_agent".to_owned()]);
    }

    #[test]
    fn default_config_asserts_the_platform_service_identity() {
        let config = GrpcAgentBridgeConfig::default();
        assert!(!config.service_subject.is_empty());
        assert!(!config.service_issuer.is_empty());
        assert!(
            config
                .service_scopes
                .iter()
                .any(|scope| scope == "execute_agent"),
            "the default identity must be able to execute agents"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn config_debug_never_renders_the_credential() {
        use mas_security::secret_string::SecretString;
        let config = GrpcAgentBridgeConfig {
            bearer_token: Some(SecretString::new("super-secret-value")),
            ..Default::default()
        };
        let rendered = format!("{config:?}");
        assert!(
            !rendered.contains("super-secret-value"),
            "a Debug dump of the config must not leak the credential: {rendered}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn empty_endpoint_is_refused() {
        let config = GrpcAgentBridgeConfig {
            endpoint: "".to_owned(),
            ..Default::default()
        };
        // `connect` is async; the endpoint guard is synchronous and reached
        // before any I/O, so assert it through the same code path.
        assert!(config.endpoint.trim().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rpc_timeout_is_bounded() {
        let config = GrpcAgentBridgeConfig::default();
        assert!(config.default_timeout >= MINIMUM_RPC_TIMEOUT);
        assert!(MAXIMUM_RPC_TIMEOUT > MINIMUM_RPC_TIMEOUT);
    }

    #[test]
    fn metadata_rejects_control_characters() {
        let mut metadata = tonic::metadata::MetadataMap::new();
        let error = insert_metadata(&mut metadata, TENANT_HEADER, "bad\nvalue")
            .expect_err("control characters must be rejected");
        assert!(matches!(error, AppError::Validation { .. }));
    }

    /// Builds a status carrying the orchestrator's structured payload, the way
    /// a Python `abort` delivers it.
    fn status_with_details(code: tonic::Code, payload: serde_json::Value) -> tonic::Status {
        let mut status = tonic::Status::new(code, "boom");
        let encoded = serde_json::to_vec(&payload).expect("payload encodes");
        status.metadata_mut().insert_bin(
            ERROR_DETAILS_METADATA_KEY,
            tonic::metadata::MetadataValue::from_bytes(&encoded),
        );
        status
    }

    #[test]
    fn peer_error_payload_is_carried_into_the_message() {
        let error = map_status(status_with_details(
            tonic::Code::FailedPrecondition,
            serde_json::json!({
                "code": "tenant_context_error",
                "message": "scope mismatch",
                "retryable": false,
                "correlation_id": "corr-7",
                "request_id": "req-9",
            }),
        ));

        let rendered = error.to_string();
        assert!(
            rendered.contains("code=tenant_context_error"),
            "the machine-readable code must survive the hop: {rendered}"
        );
        assert!(
            rendered.contains("correlation_id=corr-7"),
            "correlation id must be joinable without a second lookup: {rendered}"
        );
        assert!(
            rendered.contains("request_id=req-9"),
            "request id must be joinable: {rendered}"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_status_without_a_payload_is_unchanged() {
        // Transport failures never reach the servicer, so there is no payload.
        // The status-derived classification must stand on its own.
        let error = map_status(tonic::Status::new(tonic::Code::Unavailable, "boom"));
        assert_eq!(
            error.to_string(),
            AppError::external_service("ai-orchestrator", "orchestrator unavailable").to_string()
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_unparseable_payload_degrades_instead_of_failing() {
        let mut status = tonic::Status::new(tonic::Code::Internal, "boom");
        status.metadata_mut().insert_bin(
            ERROR_DETAILS_METADATA_KEY,
            tonic::metadata::MetadataValue::from_bytes(b"not-json"),
        );
        let error = map_status(status);
        assert!(
            !error.to_string().contains("code="),
            "a corrupt payload must not masquerade as a classification"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn peer_retryability_does_not_rewrite_the_error_kind() {
        // The orchestrator says non-retryable, but RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED is a
        // RateLimited error. Rewriting it would trade correct typing for a
        // boolean; the divergence is logged instead.
        let error = map_status(status_with_details(
            tonic::Code::ResourceExhausted,
            serde_json::json!({"code": "quota_exceeded", "retryable": false}),
        ));
        assert!(
            matches!(error, AppError::RateLimited(_)),
            "variant must keep its meaning: {error:?}"
        );
        assert!(error.is_retryable());
    }

    #[test]
    fn cancellation_code_matches_the_orchestrator_vocabulary() {
        // A cancellation is one condition and must carry one code whichever
        // side noticed it first, so callers can branch on it safely.
        assert_eq!(CANCELLATION_CODE, "cancellation_requested");
    }

    #[test]
    fn metadata_accepts_a_plain_value() {
        let mut metadata = tonic::metadata::MetadataMap::new();
        insert_metadata(&mut metadata, TENANT_HEADER, "tenant-1").expect("plain value");
        assert_eq!(
            metadata.get(TENANT_HEADER).and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()),
            Some("tenant-1")
        );
    }
}
```
